questions.question: A car suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk your horn and brake hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car cuts in front of you, release the gas pedal. This creates space between you and the other car without forcing you to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: When should you NOT point your wheels straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a red light.
When parked on a hill or slope.
When parked on a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or slope.
questions.explanation: When parked on a hill or slope, turn your wheels so your car will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail. Keep your wheels straight when waiting to turn left at a light to prevent hitting oncoming traffic if hit from behind.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly.
Pull to the edge of the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull over to the right edge and stop. On one-way streets, move to the nearest edge.

questions.question: Which statement about medications and driving is true?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs do not harm driving if you take the right dose.
All medications prescribed by a doctor are safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines, prescription or over-the-counter, can be dangerous while driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and affect your driving. You must know how your medicine affects your driving ability.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck, you should:

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag.
Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on each side. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, turn on your hazard lights and get off the road. This helps other drivers see you and keeps you safe from traffic.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic, you should:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the car ahead.
Speed up and let other vehicles move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check behind you and watch the car ahead. Always look for traffic to the side and behind your car before changing lanes.

questions.question: To turn quickly, your hands should be:

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the wheel.
At the top and bottom of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is safe and allows you to turn quickly.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must come to a complete stop, regardless of which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop and check for traffic from both directions before proceeding.
Let other traffic go first before you proceed.
Keep a steady speed and check for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic go first before you proceed.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop if needed to let other vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians pass. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light is in their favor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians near your vehicle at all times. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what the situation is.

questions.question: When can you leave a vehicle's engine running after all passengers get out?

options.text: Never.
If you will only be away for a couple minutes.
If you will be away for less than an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must turn off the engine and remove the key when you leave your vehicle. Always lock your car when you leave, even if you will only be gone a short time.

questions.question: When must you use your low beam headlights?

options.text: On a lit street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off wet surfaces and create glare that makes it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead has many curves.
There is a sharp curve ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a deep puddle on the road?

options.text: Keep your speed to get through the water quickly.
Avoid the puddle if you can.
Shift into neutral as you go through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles to prevent skidding. The safest driving surface is dry and solid.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck driver has enough space to stop.
So other drivers can slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck driver has enough space to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Never pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is 35 mph after the curve.
Drive at least 35 mph around the upcoming curve.
Slow down to 35 mph or less before the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to 35 mph or less before the curve.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs tell you about hazards ahead. Speed plaques on these signs show the safe speed for the upcoming turn.

questions.question: You are on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Stay close in bad weather because the driver can see farther than you.
Keep more distance than you would behind a regular car.
Stay one car length back so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep more distance than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck and cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you. Tailgating removes your safety cushion if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: When you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your speed the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs warn you of workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. Slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean for passing?

options.text: You can pass from both directions.
You can pass only from your direction.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: Cars keep passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: Use the right lanes on highways with four or more lanes. Only use the left lane for passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than the traffic around you, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Speed up to keep your spot.
Keep your position no matter what.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room in your lane to help other vehicles merge.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and look both ways, then go carefully.
Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and look both ways, then go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to slow down. Check for traffic crossing in front of you and continue with caution.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?

options.text: Both directions can pass.
Only the car next to the broken line can pass.
Only the car next to the solid line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only the car next to the broken line can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic going opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: After rain for several hours.
When rain just starts.
After one to two hours of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain just starts.
questions.explanation: The road is most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with water to create a slippery film.

questions.question: A school bus has red lights flashing. When can you start driving again?

options.text: When all children get off the bus.
When the stop arm folds in.
When the stop arm folds in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the stop arm folds in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: Stay stopped until the red lights turn off, the stop arm retracts, and the bus begins moving again.

questions.question: You need to park where parking is not normal. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your reverse lights on.
Park where drivers coming from any direction can see your car.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park where drivers coming from any direction can see your car.
questions.explanation: Make sure your parked car is visible to all drivers nearby, no matter which direction they are coming from.

questions.question: When must you let pedestrians in a crosswalk go first?

options.text: Only if they wave at you first.
Only if they are not using a phone.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Stop completely to let pedestrians cross. Only move forward when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: A traffic light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. What do you do?

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic light.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they go against traffic signs, signals, or road markings.

questions.question: What shape and color are construction zone signs?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow.
Diamond or rectangular with orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond or rectangular with orange and black.
questions.explanation: All work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. You will see them on the right side of the road, or both sides on divided highways.
